sentences.text: The only known fossil of Kaprosuchus is a nearly complete skull found in the Upper Cretaceous Echkar Formation of Niger.
This skull measures about 507 mm in length, while the lower jaw extends to 603 mm.
Scientists estimate the total body length of this animal ranged from 2.42 to 3.77 meters.
It possessed three sets of tusk-like caniniform teeth projecting above and below the skull, with one lower tooth fitting into notches in the upper jaw.
The eye sockets opened laterally and were angled slightly more forward than upward.
Some estimates suggest the total length of Kaprosuchus could have reached around 6 meters.
The name Kaprosuchus means boar crocodile because its unusually large caniniform teeth resemble those of a boar.
Kaprosuchus was once thought to be a primarily or exclusively terrestrial predator.
Researchers believe Kaprosuchus was a primarily, if not exclusively, terrestrial predator.
Evidence for terrestrial behavior includes the lateral and slightly forward position of the eyes, suggesting stereoscopic vision.
Fused nasal bones in Kaprosuchus are thought to have reinforced the jaws against compression from a powerful bite.
The telescoped, dorsally positioned external nares of Kaprosuchus are seen as protection against impact when ramming prey.
Due to a long retroarticular process, Kaprosuchus's jaws were likely capable of opening rapidly with a large gape to allow opposing canines sufficient space.
Kaprosuchus possessed enormous canine-like teeth with sharp edges that were relatively straight, unlike the recurved, conical, and striated teeth of aquatic crocodylomorphs.
Dorsally positioned external nostrles would have protected Kaprosuchus from impacts if it charged prey with its robust snout.
A keratinous shield believed to cover the snout tip may have provided additional protection for Kaprosuchus.
Kaprosuchus is a member of the family Mahajangasuchidae, closely related to Mahajangasuchus insignis.
Further studies show that Mahajangasuchidae form a sister clade to peirosaurids, grouping with uruguaysuchids as an early diverging branch of notosuchians.
The parent group of Kaprosuchus is the family Mahajangasuchidae.
Kaprosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Kaprosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Cenomanian age.
Kaprosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
